note: Flat faces of the Nezu jue (KIT.md § Flat faces). ONE photograph (photo-02), a three-quarter from behind the handle. The cup is ROUND: each face is a plane through the band at θ 128 seen down the photograph's own line of sight (camera θ 122, 12° up, ≈ 1.3 m, 10° lens — solved from 8 landmarks: two leg tips, two post caps, spout and tail tips, the θ 180 flange's ends; rms ≈ 16 px), so the flattened photo is close to an orthographic projection and the model is rendered down the same normal: both foreshorten the curved wall alike. Points are model surface points (band borders at θ 95 / 122 / 150 / 178) projected through that camera and slid along the line of sight onto the plane. Scale is INFERRED (band height 37.5 mm, cup Ø 69 mm).

photo-02.note: owner's photograph: three-quarter from behind the handle (camera θ ≈ 122), ≈ 12° above the band

face-band.label: the band from the handle (θ 90) to the tail flange (θ 180): half of the tail-side mask (photo-02)
face-band.trust: good from θ 105 to 170 (the wall within ±11 mm of the plane, foreshortening < 1.6:1); beyond θ 170 the wall turns away (the flange half and the nose column are squeezed ≈ 3:1) and under the handle (θ 90–100) it is hidden. Camera solve ≈ 16 px rms ≈ 2 mm.

face-upper.label: upper wall over the band: the decorated triangle, the hole (a casting flaw?) over the handle, the plain field under the tail (photo-02)
face-upper.trust: fair: the upper wall flares out from r 34.7 to ≈ 44 at the rim, so its top leans ≈ 25° back from the band's plane; positions near the rim are a few mm off.
